# Introduction

This document contains code to enable reproducibility of the paper "Less is More? Testing the Impact of Environmental Variable Refinement on Palaeolithic Site Location Models".

For this, it is necessary to execute the steps shown in the following lines.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  eval = TRUE,          
  echo = TRUE,           
  message = FALSE,       
  warning = FALSE,       
  results = 'hide',      
  fig.show = 'hide'      
)
```

# Necessary packages

Import the packages to execute the following analysis.

```{r}
# ipak function: install and load multiple R packages.
# check to see if packages are installed. Install them if they are not, then load them into the R session.

ipak <- function(pkg){
  new.pkg <- pkg[!(pkg %in% installed.packages()[, "Package"])]
  if (length(new.pkg)) 
    install.packages(new.pkg, dependencies = TRUE)
  sapply(pkg, require, character.only = TRUE)
}
# usage
packages <- c("sf", "sp", "raster", "terra", "spatstat", "spatstat.geom", 
              "spatstat.convert", "GGally", "writexl", "dplyr", "broom", 
              "tidyterra", "ggplot2", "foreach", "tibble", "magrittr", 
              "brglm2", "pROC", "patchwork", "cowplot", "ggspatial", 
              "virtualspecies", "onpoint")
ipak(packages)
```


# Import data

Import the data used.

```{r}
# set your working directory
setwd("~/spatial_patterns/shp")

# add the study areas
area_monforte  <- st_read("area_monforte.shp")
area_northern  <- st_read("area_northern.shp")
area_central   <- st_read("area_central.shp")

# add the sites
sitesSubM <- st_read("sites_monforte.shp")
sitesSubN <- st_read("sites_northern.shp")
sitesSubC  <- st_read("sites_central.shp")

# add the random sites
random_sites_monforte <- st_read("random_sites_monforte.shp")
random_sites_northern <- st_read("random_sites_northern.shp")
random_sites_central  <- st_read("random_sites_central.shp")

# set a window for each area
window_monforte <- as.owin(area_monforte)
window_north    <- as.owin(area_northern)
window_central  <- as.owin(area_central)

# create a ppp object
sitesSubM.ppp <- ppp(x = sitesSubM$UTMX, y = sitesSubM$UTMY, window = window_monforte)
sitesSubN.ppp <- ppp(x = sitesSubN$utmx, y = sitesSubN$utmy, window = window_north)
sitesSubC.ppp <- ppp(x = sitesSubC$utmx, y = sitesSubC$utmy, window = window_central)

# CSR Analysis
## Monforte de Lemos basin
### Normality test for sites
shapiro.test(sitesSubM$UTMX)

### Normality test for random sites
shapiro.test(random_sites_monforte$UTMX)

### If the alternative hypothesis is accepted, the points do not follow a normal distribution. To verify this, the K-S Test is used.
### K-S is a non-parametric test to check if the points of both samples belong to the same population.
ks.test(sitesSubM$UTMX,random_sites_monforte$UTMX)


## Northern Mountain ranges
### Normality test for sites
shapiro.test(sitesSubN$utmx)

### Normality test for random sites
shapiro.test(random_sites_northern$utmx)

### If the alternative hypothesis is accepted, the points do not follow a normal distribution. To verify this, the K-S Test is used.
### K-S is a non-parametric test to check if the points of both samples belong to the same population.
ks.test(sitesSubN$utmx,random_sites_northern$utmx)


## Central Mountain ranges
### Normality test for sites
shapiro.test(sitesSubC$utmx)

### Normality test for random sites
shapiro.test(random_sites_central$utmx)

### K-S Test
ks.test(sitesSubC$utmx,random_sites_central$utmx)
```

# Person’s Correlation function

Calculated to identify and exclude highly collinear environmental variables.

```{r}
# Person’s Correlation function
## change your working directory
setwd("~/spatial_patterns/csv")

# import data
dat_monf  <- read.table("dat_monf.csv", header = TRUE, sep = ";", dec = ".", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
dat_north <- read.table("dat_north.csv", header = TRUE, sep = ";", dec = ".", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
dat_cent  <- read.table("dat_cent.csv", header = TRUE, sep = ";", dec = ".", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

vars <- c("altitude", "wetland_cost", "goat_cost", "geology_cost", 
          "hydrology_cost", "lcp_cost", "eucl_dist_geo", "eucl_dist_hydro",
          "dif_ins", "dir_ins", "tot_ins", "aspect", "slope", 
          "vis_prom", "tpi100", "tpi500", "tpi1000", "wind")


# Data
sample_monf  <- dat_monf[, vars]
sample_north <- dat_north[, vars]
sample_cent  <- dat_cent[, vars]

# Check correlations
cor(sample_monf)
cor(sample_north)
cor(sample_cent)

# Export to csv
cor_monf <- cor(sample_monf)
write.csv2(cor_monf, file = "cor_monforte.csv", row.names = TRUE)

cor_north <- cor(sample_north)
write.csv2(cor_north, file = "cor_north.csv", row.names = TRUE)

cor_cent <- cor(sample_cent)
write.csv2(cor_cent, file = "cor_cent.csv", row.names = TRUE)

# Check correlations as scatterplots, distributions and correlation coefficient.
ggpairs(sample_monf)
ggpairs(sample_north)
ggpairs(sample_cent)

# Visualization
ggcorr(sample_monf, method=c("everything", "pearson"))
ggcorr(sample_north, method=c("everything", "pearson"))
ggcorr(sample_cent, method=c("everything", "pearson"))

```

# Resampling analysis

A Monte Carlo resampling procedure (N = 999) was performed to compare the empirical distribution of archaeological sites against the background landscape using Kernel Density Estimation and Mann-Whitney U tests.

```{r}
# Northern area

## set your working directory

# create a ppp object
coords_points  <- sf::st_coordinates(sitesSubN)
sitesSubN.ppp  <- ppp(x = sitesSubN$utmx, y = sitesSubN$utmy, window = window_north)

HYDROE_northern  <- rast("HYDROE_northern.tif")
HYDROC_northern  <- rast("HYDROC_northern.tif")
WET_northern     <- rast("WET_northern.tif")

GEOLC_northern   <- rast("GEOLC_northern.tif")

LCPC_northern    <- rast("LCPC_northern.tif")
TOTINS_northern  <- rast("TOTINS_northern.asc")
DIRINS_northern  <- rast("DIRINS_northern.asc")
DIFINS_northern  <- rast("DIFINS_northern.asc")
WIND_northern    <- rast("WIND_northern.asc")

## Raster list
rasters_north <- list(
  ALTA      = terra::rast("ALTA_northern.tif"),
  TPI100    = terra::rast("TPI100_northern.asc"),
  TPI500    = terra::rast("TPI500_northern.asc"),

  SLO       = terra::rast("SLO_northern.tif"),
  ASP       = terra::rast("ASP_northern.tif"),
  HYDROE    = terra::rast("HYDROE_northern.tif"),
  HYDROC    = terra::rast("HYDROC_northern.tif"),
  WET       = terra::rast("WET_northern.tif"),

# set your working directory
setwd("~/spatial_patterns/shp")

# add the study area and sites
area_north_vect  <- terra::vect("area_northern.shp")

area_north_vect  <- terra::project(area_north_vect,  "EPSG:25829")
sites_north_vect <- terra::project(sites_north_vect, "EPSG:25829")


## Function

run_mwu <- function(r, sites_vect, area_vect, n_iter = 999) {
  

# Force areas and sites to have the exact CRS of the raster
crs_r        <- terra::crs(r)
area_vect    <- terra::project(area_vect,  crs_r)
sites_vect   <- terra::project(sites_vect, crs_r)
  
# Clip and mask the raster to the study area
r_mask <- terra::mask(terra::crop(r, area_vect), area_vect)
  
# Background values within the area
background_values <- terra::values(r_mask, mat = FALSE, na.rm = TRUE)
  
# Raster values at the sites
site_values <- terra::extract(r, sites_vect, ID = FALSE, na.rm = TRUE)[, 1]
site_values <- site_values[!is.na(site_values)]
  
n_sites <- length(site_values)
  
# n_iter tests Mann-Whitney U
mwu_results <- foreach(n = 1:n_iter, .combine = rbind) %do% {
  background_sample <- sample(background_values, n_sites, replace = FALSE)
    
  wilcox.test(x = site_values,
              y = background_sample,
              alternative = "greater",
              exact = FALSE) %>%
    broom::tidy() %>%
    tibble::as_tibble()
} %>%
  dplyr::select(statistic, p.value)
  
# Median and IC 95%
summary_res <- foreach::foreach(prob = c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975), .combine = rbind) %do% {
  mwu_results %>%
    dplyr::summarise_all(quantile, probs = prob)
} %>%
  t() %>%
  magrittr::set_colnames(c("Lower CI", "Median", "Upper CI")) %>%
  magrittr::set_rownames(c("U statistic", "p-value"))
  
  return(summary_res)
}

analyse_area <- function(rasters_area, sites_vect, area_vect, area_name, output_file, n_iter = 999) {
  message("Processing area: ", area_name, " ...")
  results_list <- lapply(names(rasters_area), function(variable) {
    res <- run_mwu(
      r          = rasters_area[[variable]],
      sites_vect = sites_vect,
      area_vect  = area_vect,
      n_iter     = n_iter
    )
    res_df <- as.data.frame(res)
    res_df$Variable  <- variable
    res_df$Statistic <- rownames(res_df)
    res_df
  })
  results_table <- do.call(rbind, results_list)
  results_table <- results_table %>%
    dplyr::select(Variable, Statistic, `Lower CI`, Median, `Upper CI`) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 4)))
  dir.create(dirname(output_file), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  writexl::write_xlsx(results_table, path = output_file)
  message("  -> Saved: ", output_file)
  return(results_table)
}

set.seed(123)   

results_northern <- analyse_area(
  rasters_area = rasters_north,        # 19 rasters list
  sites_vect   = sites_north_vect,     # sites SpatVector 
  area_vect    = area_north_vect,      # area SpatVector 
  area_name    = "Northern",
  output_file  = "~/outputs/MWU_Northern.xlsx",
  n_iter       = 999
)

print(results_northern)

## Function

run_mwu <- function(r, sites_vect, area_vect, n_iter = 999) {
  
  
  # Force areas and sites to have the exact CRS of the raster
  crs_r        <- terra::crs(r)
  area_vect    <- terra::project(area_vect,  crs_r)
  sites_vect   <- terra::project(sites_vect, crs_r)
  
  # Clip and mask the raster to the study area
  r_mask <- terra::mask(terra::crop(r, area_vect), area_vect)
  
  # Background values within the area
  background_values <- terra::values(r_mask, mat = FALSE, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # Raster values at the sites
  site_values <- terra::extract(r, sites_vect, ID = FALSE, na.rm = TRUE)[, 1]
  site_values <- site_values[!is.na(site_values)]
  
  n_sites <- length(site_values)
  
  # n_iter tests Mann-Whitney U
  mwu_results <- foreach(n = 1:n_iter, .combine = rbind) %do% {
    background_sample <- sample(background_values, n_sites, replace = FALSE)
    
    wilcox.test(x = site_values,
                y = background_sample,
                alternative = "greater",
                exact = FALSE) %>%
      broom::tidy() %>%
      tibble::as_tibble()
  } %>%
    dplyr::select(statistic, p.value)
  
  # Median and IC 95%
  summary_res <- foreach::foreach(prob = c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975), .combine = rbind) %do% {
    mwu_results %>%
      dplyr::summarise_all(quantile, probs = prob)
  } %>%
    t() %>%
    magrittr::set_colnames(c("Lower CI", "Median", "Upper CI")) %>%
    magrittr::set_rownames(c("U statistic", "p-value"))
  
  return(summary_res)
}

  crs_r        <- terra::crs(r)
  area_vect    <- terra::project(area_vect,  crs_r)
  sites_vect   <- terra::project(sites_vect, crs_r)
  
  # Clip and mask the raster to the study area
  r_mask <- terra::mask(terra::crop(r, area_vect), area_vect)
  
  # Background values within the area
  background_values <- terra::values(r_mask, mat = FALSE, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # Raster values at the sites
  site_values <- terra::extract(r, sites_vect, ID = FALSE, na.rm = TRUE)[, 1]
  site_values <- site_values[!is.na(site_values)]
  
  n_sites <- length(site_values)
  
  # n_iter tests Mann-Whitney U
  mwu_results <- foreach(n = 1:n_iter, .combine = rbind) %do% {
    background_sample <- sample(background_values, n_sites, replace = FALSE)
    
    wilcox.test(x = site_values,
                y = background_sample,
                alternative = "greater",
                exact = FALSE) %>%
      broom::tidy() %>%
      tibble::as_tibble()
  } %>%
    dplyr::select(statistic, p.value)
  
  # Median and IC 95%
  summary_res <- foreach::foreach(prob = c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975), .combine = rbind) %do% {
    mwu_results %>%
      dplyr::summarise_all(quantile, probs = prob)
  } %>%
    t() %>%
    magrittr::set_colnames(c("Lower CI", "Median", "Upper CI")) %>%
    magrittr::set_rownames(c("U statistic", "p-value"))
  
  return(summary_res)
}

set.seed(123)   

results_monforte <- analyse_area(
  rasters_area = rasters_monforte,        # 19 rasters list
  sites_vect   = sites_monforte_vect,     # sites SpatVector 
  area_vect    = area_monforte_vect,      # area SpatVector 
  area_name    = "monforte",
  output_file  = "~/outputs/MWU_Monforte.xlsx",
  n_iter       = 999
)

print(results_monforte)
```


## GLM

Generalized Linear Models (GLM) with Firth's penalized likelihood were fitted to generate predictive probability surfaces, with optimal covariates selected via backward stepwise AIC


```{r}
# GLM Monforte

# add the sites
setwd("~/spatial_patterns/shp")

locations_monf <- terra::vect("locations_monforte.shp")

## raster directory
setwd("~/spatial_patterns/grids")

## add reference raster
elevation <- terra::rast("ALTA_monforte.tif")

## add rasters
tot_inso    <- terra::project(terra::rast("TOTINS_monforte.asc"), elevation)
aspect      <- terra::project(terra::rast("ASP_monforte.tif"),          elevation)
slope       <- terra::project(terra::rast("SLO_monforte.tif"),           elevation)
visual_prom <- terra::project(terra::rast("VISPR_monforte.tif"), elevation)
tpi100      <- terra::project(terra::rast("TPI100_monforte.asc"),          elevation)
wind        <- terra::project(terra::rast("WIND_monforte.asc"),            elevation)
wetland_cost <- terra::project(terra::rast("WET_monforte.tiff"),  elevation)
geol_cost    <- terra::project(terra::rast("GEOLC_monforte.tiff"),  elevation)
hydro_cost   <- terra::project(terra::rast("HYDROC_monforte.tiff"), elevation)
lcp_cost     <- terra::project(terra::rast("LCPC_monforte.tiff"),      elevation)
cost_goats     <- terra::project(terra::rast("CPFPCGc_monforte.tif"),      elevation)


## create stack
covariates_monf <- c(elevation, tot_inso, aspect, slope, visual_prom, tpi100,
                wetland_cost, geol_cost, hydro_cost, lcp_cost, wind)

names(covariates_monf) <- c("elevation", "tot_inso", "aspect", "slope",
                       "visual_prom", "tpi100", "wetland_cost",
                       "geol_cost", "hydro_cost", "lcp_cost", "wind")

## extract values
locvals_monf <- as.data.frame(terra::extract(covariates_monf, locations_monf, ID = FALSE))

## Response variable: 1 if the point is an archaeological site
locvals_monf$site <- as.integer(locations_monf$CID == 1)

## fit de GLM
mod_monf <- glm(site ~ elevation + tot_inso + aspect + slope + visual_prom +
             tpi100 + wetland_cost + geol_cost + hydro_cost + lcp_cost + wind,
           data = locvals_monf, family = binomial(link = "logit"), method = brglm2::brglmFit)

summary(mod_monf)

## AIC selection
mod2_monf <- step(mod_monf, direction = "backward")
mod2_monf$anova
summary(mod2_monf)

## relative probability (predict type = "response")
relprob_monf <- terra::predict(covariates_monf, mod2_monf, type = "response", na.rm = TRUE)

## Visualization
plot(relprob_monf, col = terrain.colors(8, alpha = 1), legend = TRUE,
     axes = TRUE, main = "GLM Monforte")
plot(locations_monf[locations_monf$CID == 1, ], pch = 19, cex = 0.3, col = "red", add = TRUE)

## export surface
setwd("~/spatial_patterns/outputs")

terra::writeRaster(relprob_monf,
                   filename = "predicsurface_monforte.asc",
                   filetype = "AAIGrid",
                   NAflag = -9999,
                   overwrite = TRUE)

writeLines(terra::crs(relprob_monf, proj = TRUE),
           "predicsurface_northern.prj")


## Model Validation

## Import validation sample
setwd("~/spatial_patterns/shp")
val_monf <- terra::vect("control_sample_monforte.shp")

## Verification
cat("=== Monforte: validation composition ===\n")
print(table(val_monf$CID))
cat("Total points:", nrow(val_monf), "\n\n")

## Extract predictions from the raster
val_pred_monf <- terra::extract(relprob_monf, val_monf, ID = FALSE)[, 1]

cat("NA in predictions:", sum(is.na(val_pred_monf)), "\n\n")

## Calculate sensitivity, specificity, and AUC
pred_sites  <- val_pred_monf[val_monf$CID == 1]
pred_random <- val_pred_monf[val_monf$CID == 0]

sens <- mean(pred_sites  > 0.5, na.rm = TRUE) * 100
spec <- mean(pred_random < 0.5, na.rm = TRUE) * 100

cat("N validation sites:", length(pred_sites), "\n")
cat("N validation control:", length(pred_random), "\n")
cat("Sensibility (> 0.5):", round(sens, 1), "%\n")
cat("Specificity (< 0.5):", round(spec, 1), "%\n")

roc_obj <- roc(
  response  = c(rep(1, length(pred_sites)), rep(0, length(pred_random))),
  predictor = c(pred_sites, pred_random),
  quiet     = TRUE
)
cat("AUC:", round(auc(roc_obj), 3), "\n")
```

## Kernel Density Estimations

Kernel density estimations were generated to visually compare the distribution of environmental variables at archaeological sites against 999 Monte Carlo resamples of the background landscape.

```{r}
# Kernel Density Estimation - Northern area

## add the sites
setwd("~/spatial_patterns/shp")
sites_north <- terra::vect("sites_northern.shp")

## Kernel density Function + MWU for each variable
kernel_density_plot <- function(raster_file, sites, variable_name,
                                area_name, n_iter = 999, n_grid = 256) {
  
  r <- terra::rast(raster_file)
  
  ## Force sites to the raster CRS (removes [extract] transforming warning)
  sites <- terra::project(sites, terra::crs(r))
  
  ## Sites values
  site_values <- terra::extract(r, sites, ID = FALSE)[, 1]
  site_values <- site_values[!is.na(site_values)]
  n_sites <- length(site_values)
  
  ## Check variation (e.g., CPFPCDc all zero in Northern)
  no_variation <- diff(range(site_values)) == 0
  if (no_variation) {
    warning("Variable ", variable_name, ": sites have no variation (all = ",
            unique(site_values)[1], "). MWU will be skipped.")
  }
  
  ## Background values (entire area, rasters already cropped)
  background_values <- terra::values(r, mat = FALSE, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  ## Common range for density
  rng <- range(background_values, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  ## Sites density
  dens_sites <- density(site_values, from = rng[1], to = rng[2], n = n_grid)
  sites_df <- data.frame(x = dens_sites$x, y = dens_sites$y * n_sites)
  
  ## 999 background simulations
  bg_dens <- replicate(n_iter, {
    sample_vals <- sample(background_values, n_sites, replace = FALSE)
    d <- density(sample_vals, from = rng[1], to = rng[2], n = n_grid)
    data.frame(x = d$x, y = d$y * n_sites)
  }, simplify = FALSE)
  
  bg_df <- bind_rows(bg_dens) %>%
    group_by(x) %>%
    summarise(
      lower  = quantile(y, 0.025),
      median = quantile(y, 0.5),
      upper  = quantile(y, 0.975),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  
  ## Plot
  p <- ggplot() +
    geom_line(data = bg_df, aes(x = x, y = median)) +
    geom_ribbon(data = bg_df, aes(x = x, ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
                alpha = 0.3) +
    geom_line(data = sites_df, aes(x = x, y = y), color = "red") +
    labs(title = paste0(variable_name, " in ", area_name),
         x = variable_name, y = "Frequency") +
    theme_bw()
  
  ## MWU companion (skipped if no variation)
  if (no_variation) {
    mwu_summary <- data.frame(
      Metric = c("U statistic", "p-value"),
      Lower  = c(NA_real_, NA_real_),
      Median = c(NA_real_, NA_real_),
      Upper  = c(NA_real_, NA_real_)
    )
  } else {
    mwu <- replicate(n_iter, {
      sample_vals <- sample(background_values, n_sites, replace = FALSE)
      wilcox.test(x = site_values, y = sample_vals,
                  alternative = "two.sided", exact = FALSE) %>%
        broom::tidy()
    }, simplify = FALSE) %>%
      bind_rows()
    
    mwu <- mwu[, c("statistic", "p.value")]   # subsetting, evita terra::select
    
    ## Safety net: drop any non-finite values
    mwu_clean <- mwu[is.finite(mwu$statistic) & is.finite(mwu$p.value), ]
    
    mwu_summary <- data.frame(
      Metric = c("U statistic", "p-value"),
      Lower  = as.numeric(c(quantile(mwu_clean$statistic, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
                            quantile(mwu_clean$p.value,   0.025, na.rm = TRUE))),
      Median = as.numeric(c(median(mwu_clean$statistic, na.rm = TRUE),
                            median(mwu_clean$p.value,   na.rm = TRUE))),
      Upper  = as.numeric(c(quantile(mwu_clean$statistic, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE),
                            quantile(mwu_clean$p.value,   0.975, na.rm = TRUE)))
    )
  }
  
  list(plot = p, mwu = mwu_summary, sites = sites_df, background = bg_df)
}

# Kernel Density Estimation - Monforte

## add the sites
setwd("~/spatial_patterns/shp")
sites_monf <- terra::vect("sites_monforte.shp")

## Kernel density Function + MWU for each variable
kernel_density_plot <- function(raster_file, sites, variable_name,
                                area_name, n_iter = 999, n_grid = 256) {
  
  r <- terra::rast(raster_file)
  
  ## Force sites to the raster CRS
  sites <- terra::project(sites, terra::crs(r))
  
  ## Sites values
  site_values <- terra::extract(r, sites, ID = FALSE)[, 1]
  site_values <- site_values[!is.na(site_values)]
  n_sites <- length(site_values)
  
  ## Check variation
  no_variation <- diff(range(site_values)) == 0
  if (no_variation) {
    warning("Variable ", variable_name, ": sites have no variation (all = ",
            unique(site_values)[1], "). MWU will be skipped.")
  }
  
  ## Background values
  background_values <- terra::values(r, mat = FALSE, na.rm = TRUE)
  rng <- range(background_values, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  ## Sites density
  dens_sites <- density(site_values, from = rng[1], to = rng[2], n = n_grid)
  sites_df <- data.frame(x = dens_sites$x, y = dens_sites$y * n_sites)
  
  ## 999 background simulations
  bg_dens <- replicate(n_iter, {
    sample_vals <- sample(background_values, n_sites, replace = FALSE)
    d <- density(sample_vals, from = rng[1], to = rng[2], n = n_grid)
    data.frame(x = d$x, y = d$y * n_sites)
  }, simplify = FALSE)
  
  bg_df <- bind_rows(bg_dens) %>%
    group_by(x) %>%
    summarise(
      lower  = quantile(y, 0.025),
      median = quantile(y, 0.5),
      upper  = quantile(y, 0.975),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  
  ## Plot
  p <- ggplot() +
    geom_line(data = bg_df, aes(x = x, y = median)) +
    geom_ribbon(data = bg_df, aes(x = x, ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
                alpha = 0.3) +
    geom_line(data = sites_df, aes(x = x, y = y), color = "red") +
    labs(title = paste0(variable_name, " in ", area_name),
         x = variable_name, y = "Frequency") +
    theme_bw()
  
  ## MWU companion
  if (no_variation) {
    mwu_summary <- data.frame(
      Metric = c("U statistic", "p-value"),
      Lower  = c(NA_real_, NA_real_),
      Median = c(NA_real_, NA_real_),
      Upper  = c(NA_real_, NA_real_)
    )
  } else {
    mwu <- replicate(n_iter, {
      sample_vals <- sample(background_values, n_sites, replace = FALSE)
      wilcox.test(x = site_values, y = sample_vals,
                  alternative = "two.sided", exact = FALSE) %>%
        broom::tidy()
    }, simplify = FALSE) %>%
      bind_rows()
    
    mwu <- mwu[, c("statistic", "p.value")]
    mwu_clean <- mwu[is.finite(mwu$statistic) & is.finite(mwu$p.value), ]
    
    mwu_summary <- data.frame(
      Metric = c("U statistic", "p-value"),
      Lower  = as.numeric(c(quantile(mwu_clean$statistic, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
                            quantile(mwu_clean$p.value,   0.025, na.rm = TRUE))),
      Median = as.numeric(c(median(mwu_clean$statistic, na.rm = TRUE),
                            median(mwu_clean$p.value,   na.rm = TRUE))),
      Upper  = as.numeric(c(quantile(mwu_clean$statistic, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE),
                            quantile(mwu_clean$p.value,   0.975, na.rm = TRUE)))
    )
  }
  
  list(plot = p, mwu = mwu_summary, sites = sites_df, background = bg_df)
}
```

## Refinement

Spatial point pattern analysis and inhomogeneous Pair Correlation Functions (PCF) were applied to evaluate the extent to which first-order environmental variables and second-order spatial interactions explain site clustering.

```{r}
# Refinement Monforte

# set the working directory
setwd("~/spatial_patterns/shp")

# Load vector data
gg <- st_read("sites_monforte.shp", quiet = TRUE)

p <- st_read("area_monforte.shp", quiet = TRUE)

wind <- as.owin(p)

gp <- unmark(as.ppp(gg))

gpw <- gp[wind]

# Load and prepare raster data

# set de wd
setwd("~/spatial_patterns/grids")

dem <- raster("ALTA_monforte.tif")
slo <- raster("SLO_monforte.tif")
vis <- raster("VISPR_monforte.tif")

slo <- resample(slo, dem)
vis <- resample(vis, dem)

rs <- stack(dem, slo, vis)  

removeCollinearity(rs, multicollinearity.cutoff = 0.75,
                   select.variables = FALSE, sample.points = TRUE, nb.points = 100000,
                   plot = TRUE) # No collinear variables

gvars <- list(as.im(as(dem, "SpatialGridDataFrame")),
              as.im(as(slo, "SpatialGridDataFrame")),
              as.im(as(vis, "SpatialGridDataFrame")))

names(gvars) <- c("dem", "slo", "vis")

rm(dem)
rm(slo)
rm(vis)
rm(rs)

# Extract data frame

marea <- as.ppp(gg)
datproj <- as.data.frame(marea)

## Analysis: Model fitting

# First order

gtrend <- ~ dem + slo + vis # Define spatial trend

fitgg <- step(ppm(gpw, trend = gtrend, covariates=gvars, correction = "iso", method="logi"), k=log(5))

summary(fitgg)

# First and second order

gatrend <- ~ dem + slo + vis

ir <- data.frame(r=seq(100, 2500, by=100))

fitgg2 <- profilepl(ir, f=AreaInter, gpw, aic=TRUE, fast=TRUE, covariates=gvars, trend=gatrend, verbose=TRUE)

# profilepl() is used over ppm() due to the lack of parallelisation of this function
# and hence the extreme length of time it takes to fit and output. Results are equivalent.

pt <- as.ppm(fitgg2)

## Analysis: Model testing

# Based on 999 simulations of CSR - this may take a while to run.

# Null

null <- envelope(gpw, fun = pcfinhom, nsim = 999, correction = "iso", divisor="d")

# First order 

gsimfit <- envelope(fitgg, fun = pcfinhom, nsim = 999, correction="iso", divisor = "d")

# First and second order

gsimfit2 <- envelope(pt, fun = pcfinhom, nsim = 999, correction="iso", divisor = "d", method="logi")


# create heterogenous pattern
null_model_hetero <- rheteroppp(gpw, nsim = 999)

hetero <- envelope(gpw, fun = pcf, 
                   funargs = list(correction = "Ripley", divisor = "d"),
                   simulate = null_model_hetero, nsim = 999, 
                   verbose = FALSE)


# Create Figure ginhom function
p1 <- plot_quantums(hetero, 
                    xlab = "Distance between points (r)",
                    ylab = "ginhom(r)",
                    labels=c("Regular pattern", 
                             "Random pattern", 
                             "Clustered pattern"),
                    title="a. Simulated heterogeneous pattern model") 

p2 <- plot_quantums(null, 
                    xlab = "Distance between points (r)",
                    ylab = "ginhom(r)",
                    labels=c("Regular pattern", 
                             "Random pattern", 
                             "Clustered pattern"),
                    title="b. Null model") 

p3 <- plot_quantums(gsimfit, 
                    xlab = "Distance between points (r)",
                    ylab = "ginhom(r)",
                    labels=c("Regular pattern", 
                             "Random pattern", 
                             "Clustered pattern"),
                    title="c. First-order effects model") 

p4 <- plot_quantums(gsimfit2, 
                    xlab = "Distance between points (r)",
                    ylab = "ginhom(r)",
                    labels=c("Regular pattern", 
                             "Random pattern", 
                             "Clustered pattern"),
                    title="d. First and second-order effects model") 

(p1| p2) /
  (p3| p4)

# Load vector data
gg <- st_read("sites_central.shp", quiet = TRUE)

p <- st_read("area_central.shp", quiet = TRUE)

wind <- as.owin(p)

gp <- unmark(as.ppp(gg))

gpw <- gp[wind]

# Load and prepare raster data

# set de wd
setwd("~/spatial_patterns/grids")

dem <- raster("ALTA_central.tif")
tpi <- raster("TPI1000_central.asc")
geo <- raster("GEOLC_central.tif")

tpi <- resample(tpi, dem)
geo <- resample(geo, dem)

rs <- stack(dem, tpi, geo)  

removeCollinearity(rs, multicollinearity.cutoff = 0.75,
                   select.variables = FALSE, sample.points = TRUE, nb.points = 100000,
                   plot = TRUE) # No collinear variables

gvars <- list(as.im(as(dem, "SpatialGridDataFrame")),
              as.im(as(tpi, "SpatialGridDataFrame")),
              as.im(as(geo, "SpatialGridDataFrame")))

names(gvars) <- c("dem", "tpi", "geo")

rm(dem)
rm(tpi)
rm(geo)
rm(rs)

# Extract data frame

marea <- as.ppp(gg)
datproj <- as.data.frame(marea)

## Analysis: Model fitting

# First order

gtrend <- ~ dem + tpi + geo # Define spatial trend

fitgg <- step(ppm(gpw, trend = gtrend, covariates=gvars, correction = "iso", method="logi"), k=log(5))

summary(fitgg)

# First and second order

gatrend <- ~ dem + tpi + geo

ir <- data.frame(r=seq(100, 2500, by=100))

fitgg2 <- profilepl(ir, f=AreaInter, gpw, aic=TRUE, fast=TRUE, covariates=gvars, trend=gatrend, verbose=TRUE)

# profilepl() is used over ppm() due to the lack of parallelisation of this function
# and hence the extreme length of time it takes to fit and output. Results are equivalent.

pt <- as.ppm(fitgg2)

## Analysis: Model testing

# Based on 999 simulations of CSR - this may take a while to run.

# Null

null <- envelope(gpw, fun = pcfinhom, nsim = 999, correction = "iso", divisor="d")

# First order 

gsimfit <- envelope(fitgg, fun = pcfinhom, nsim = 999, correction="iso", divisor = "d")

# First and second order

gsimfit2 <- envelope(pt, fun = pcfinhom, nsim = 999, correction="iso", divisor = "d", method="logi")


# create heterogenous pattern
null_model_hetero <- rheteroppp(gpw, nsim = 999)

hetero <- envelope(gpw, fun = pcf, 
                   funargs = list(correction = "Ripley", divisor = "d"),
                   simulate = null_model_hetero, nsim = 999, 
                   verbose = FALSE)


# Create Figure ginhom function
p1 <- plot_quantums(hetero, 
                    xlab = "Distance between points (r)",
                    ylab = "ginhom(r)",
                    labels=c("Regular pattern", 
                             "Random pattern", 
                             "Clustered pattern"),
                    title="a. Simulated heterogeneous pattern model") 

p2 <- plot_quantums(null, 
                    xlab = "Distance between points (r)",
                    ylab = "ginhom(r)",
                    labels=c("Regular pattern", 
                             "Random pattern", 
                             "Clustered pattern"),
                    title="b. Null model") 

p3 <- plot_quantums(gsimfit, 
                    xlab = "Distance between points (r)",
                    ylab = "ginhom(r)",
                    labels=c("Regular pattern", 
                             "Random pattern", 
                             "Clustered pattern"),
                    title="c. First-order effects model") 

p4 <- plot_quantums(gsimfit2, 
                    xlab = "Distance between points (r)",
                    ylab = "ginhom(r)",
                    labels=c("Regular pattern", 
                             "Random pattern", 
                             "Clustered pattern"),
                    title="d. First and second-order effects model") 

(p1| p2) /
  (p3| p4) 
```
